_readme: The Keeper. Four bars at 120 - eight seconds, the overworld theme's length rather than
the fight's six, because a boss is the longest fight in the game and the loop that
carries it should not come round twice before the first round ends.
WHY A SECOND FIGHT THEME EXISTS AT ALL, and why it hangs off the ENEMY. The references
disagree about which fights get one, and the disagreement is the whole argument: Dragon
Quest I (1986) ships eight tracks and reserves its second battle theme for the
Dragonlord; Final Fantasy I has ONE and plays it for every fight including Chaos;
Final Fantasy II gave major bosses 'Battle Theme 2'; by IV it plays for all but two. A
field on EnemyDef sits anywhere on that range without the template choosing. See
The one place this soundtrack leaves the key with no sharps in it. Everything else here
is natural A minor; this leans on G#, the harmonic minor's raised seventh, which is what
turns the walk down to E from a cadence into a threat. It is deliberate and it is the
only file that does it - a boss should be the thing that sounds wrong.
The bass is a PEDAL in eighths rather than skirmish's alternating root and fifth: an
ordinary fight is a stand, and this is being leaned on. It moves only in bars two and
three, so the pressure lets up exactly once per loop.
Written to loop like every other track here - it ends on the dominant so the return to A
resolves, and the drum fills into the seam rather than stopping at it.
